tasks.prompt: Say what each proper name is: Zayd; Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn; Abū ʿAmr; Usāma.
tasks.answer: Zayd: a personal name (ism). Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn: a laqab. Abū ʿAmr: a kunya. Usāma: a proper name of a kind, the lion.

tasks.prompt: Why may one say Saʿīdu Kurzin with iḍāfa, but not join a laqab by iḍāfa to ʿAbd Allāh?
tasks.answer: The iḍāfa is allowed only if the name and the laqab are both single words. ʿAbd Allāh is already an iḍāfa, so the laqab after it can only follow it in its iʿrāb.

tasks.prompt: Why does the dual demonstrative change from dhāni to dhayni?
tasks.answer: It is declined like the dual: the alif in rafʿ, the yāʾ in jarr and naṣb.

quiz.prompt: Usāma, a name for the lion, is a proper name…
quiz.explanation: It names the whole kind, yet is treated as definite.

quiz.prompt: Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn is…
quiz.explanation: A nickname of praise.

quiz.prompt: A kunya is made with…
quiz.explanation: Abū ʿAmr, Umm ʿAmr.

quiz.prompt: The laqab comes…
quiz.explanation: Saʿīd Kurz: the name first.

quiz.prompt: Dhayni is used in…
quiz.explanation: Dhāni in rafʿ, dhayni in jarr and naṣb.

quiz.prompt: The demonstrative for the plural of both genders is…
quiz.explanation: Ūlāʾi, for men and for women.

quiz.prompt: Where is the lām NOT used with the far demonstrative?
quiz.explanation: Hādhāka, not hādhālika; nor in the dual.

text.original: ثُمَّ الْعَلَمُ، وَهُوَ إِمَّا شَخْصِيٌّ كَزَيْدٍ، أَوْ جِنْسِيٌّ كَأُسَامَةَ، وَإِمَّا اسْمٌ كَمَا مَثَّلْنَا، أَوْ لَقَبٌ كَزَيْنِ الْعَابِدِينَ وَقُفَّةَ، أَوْ كُنْيَةٌ كَأَبِي عَمْرٍو وَأُمِّ عَمْرٍو. وَيُؤَخَّرُ اللَّقَبُ عَنِ الِاسْمِ تَابِعًا لَهُ مُطْلَقًا، أَوْ مَخْفُوضًا بِإِضَافَتِهِ إِنْ أُفْرِدَا كَسَعِيدِ كُرْزٍ.
text.en: Then the proper name (ʿalam), which is either personal, as Zayd, or of a kind, as Usāma [a name of the lion]; and either a name (ism), as we have exemplified, or a nickname (laqab), as Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn “the adornment of the worshippers” and Quffa “basket”, or a kunya, as Abū ʿAmr “the father of ʿAmr” and Umm ʿAmr “the mother of ʿAmr”. The laqab is put after the name, following it [in its iʿrāb] in every case, or in khafḍ by iḍāfa to it if both are single, as Saʿīd Kurz.

text.original: ثُمَّ الْإِشَارَةُ، وَهِيَ ذَا لِلْمُذَكَّرِ، وَذِي وَذِهْ وَتِي وَتِهْ وَتَا لِلْمُؤَنَّثِ، وَذَانِ وَتَانِ لِلْمُثَنَّى رَفْعًا، وَذَيْنِ وَتَيْنِ جَرًّا وَنَصْبًا، وَأُولَاءِ لِجَمْعِهِمَا. وَالْبَعِيدُ بِالْكَافِ مُجَرَّدَةً مِنَ اللَّامِ مُطْلَقًا، أَوْ مَقْرُونَةً بِهَا إِلَّا فِي الْمُثَنَّى مُطْلَقًا، وَفِي الْجَمْعِ فِي لُغَةِ مَنْ مَدَّهُ، وَفِيمَا تَقَدَّمَتْهُ هَا التَّنْبِيهِ.
text.en: Then the demonstrative (ishāra): dhā for the masculine; dhī, dhih, tī, tih and tā for the feminine; dhāni and tāni for the dual in rafʿ, and dhayni and tayni in jarr and naṣb; and ūlāʾi for the plural of both. The far is [pointed at] with the kāf, either without the lām in every case, or joined with it, except in the dual in every case, in the plural in the dialect of those who lengthen it, and in what is preceded by the hā of alerting (hā al-tanbīh).

lessons.title: The relative noun and its ṣila
body: A relative noun (mawṣūl) means “the one who, that which”, and needs a clause after it, its ṣila, to complete it. Some have one form for each gender and number: alladhī and allatī; alladhāni and allatāni, with the alif in rafʿ and the yāʾ in jarr and naṣb, like the dual; for men alladhīna, “with the yāʾ in every case”, and al-ulā; for women allāʾī and allātī.

Others are shared by all: man, mā and ayyun; al- in a plain adjective that is not one of preference, as al-ḍārib, “the one who hits”, and al-maḍrūb, “the one hit”, where al-ḍārib means alladhī ḍaraba; dhū in the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ; and dhā after the interrogative mā or man, as in mādhā, “what is it that…?”.

The ṣila of al- is the adjective itself. The ṣila of the others is a declarative sentence with a pronoun that agrees with the relative, called the returner (ʿāʾid), because it returns to it. The returner may be dropped, and the book's four verses show four kinds: ayyuhum ashaddu (Q 19:69), where “huwa” before ashaddu is dropped; wa-mā ʿamilat aydīhim (Q 36:35), where the object “-hu” of ʿamilat is dropped; fa-iqḍi mā anta qāḍin (Q 20:72), where the pronoun governed by qāḍin is dropped; and wa-yashrabu mimmā tashrabūna (Q 23:33), where “minhu” is dropped after tashrabūna, since the same preposition came before the relative.

The ṣila may also be an adverb (ẓarf) or a prepositional phrase, as long as it is “complete”, giving a meaning: alladhī ʿindaka, “the one who is with you”, alladhī fī al-dāri, “the one who is in the house”. These hang on an understood istaqarra, “is settled”: “the one who is settled in the house”.

terms.en: the relative noun: “the one who, that which”
the clause that completes the relative
the returner: the pronoun in the ṣila that refers to the relative
al- as a relative, in an adjective such as al-ḍārib

examples.en: al-ḍārib, al-maḍrūb: al- as a relative, its ṣila the adjective
ayyuhum ashaddu (Q 19:69): the returner huwa dropped
wa-mā ʿamilat aydīhim (Q 36:35): the object -hu dropped
fa-iqḍi mā anta qāḍin (Q 20:72): the pronoun governed by qāḍin dropped

tasks.prompt: Which returner has been dropped in each verse, and what was its place? ayyuhum ashaddu; wa-mā ʿamilat aydīhim; wa-yashrabu mimmā tashrabūna.
tasks.arabic: أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ — وَمَا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ — وَيَشْرَبُ مِمَّا تَشْرَبُونَ
tasks.answer: Ayyuhum [huwa] ashaddu: a subject in rafʿ. Wa-mā ʿamilat[hu] aydīhim: an object in naṣb. Wa-yashrabu mimmā tashrabūna [minhu]: a pronoun in jarr, after the same preposition min that came before the relative.

tasks.prompt: Why is the al- of al-ḍārib a relative noun, and what is its ṣila?
tasks.answer: It means alladhī, “the one who”: al-ḍārib is “the one who hits”. Its ṣila is the adjective ḍārib itself; the al- of other nouns (al-rajul) is only the article.

tasks.prompt: In jāʾa alladhī fī al-dāri, what is the ṣila, and what does it hang on?
tasks.answer: The ṣila is the prepositional phrase fī al-dāri, complete in meaning. It hangs on an understood istaqarra: “the one who is settled in the house”.

quiz.prompt: The dual relative alladhāni becomes … in naṣb and jarr.
quiz.explanation: With the yāʾ, like the dual.

quiz.prompt: Alladhīna is used…
options: with the yāʾ in every case
quiz.explanation: The book: “with the yāʾ in every case”.

quiz.prompt: In al-ḍārib, al- is…
quiz.explanation: Al- in a plain adjective means alladhī.

quiz.prompt: The returner (ʿāʾid) is…
options: a pronoun in the ṣila that refers to the relative
quiz.explanation: It agrees with the relative in gender and number.

quiz.prompt: In wa-mā ʿamilat aydīhim, the dropped returner is…
quiz.explanation: Wa-mā ʿamilathu aydīhim.

quiz.prompt: Dhū is a relative noun…
quiz.explanation: Elsewhere dhū is one of the six nouns.

quiz.prompt: A ṣila that is a prepositional phrase hangs on…
quiz.explanation: Alladhī fī al-dāri: “the one who is settled in the house”.

text.original: ثُمَّ الْمَوْصُولُ، وَهُوَ الَّذِي وَالَّتِي، وَاللَّذَانِ وَاللَّتَانِ بِالْأَلِفِ رَفْعًا وَبِالْيَاءِ جَرًّا وَنَصْبًا، وَلِجَمْعِ الْمُذَكَّرِ الَّذِينَ بِالْيَاءِ مُطْلَقًا، وَالْأُلَى، وَلِجَمْعِ الْمُؤَنَّثِ اللَّائِي وَاللَّاتِي، وَبِمَعْنَى الْجَمِيعِ مَنْ وَمَا وَأَيٌّ، وَأَلْ فِي وَصْفٍ صَرِيحٍ لِغَيْرِ تَفْضِيلٍ كَالضَّارِبِ وَالْمَضْرُوبِ، وَذُو فِي لُغَةِ طَيِّئٍ، وَذَا بَعْدَ مَا أَوْ مَنِ الِاسْتِفْهَامِيَّتَيْنِ.
text.en: Then the relative (mawṣūl): alladhī and allatī; alladhāni and allatāni, with the alif in rafʿ and the yāʾ in jarr and naṣb; for the masculine plural alladhīna, with the yāʾ in every case, and al-ulā; for the feminine plural allāʾī and allātī; in the sense of all of these, man “who”, mā “what” and ayyun “which”; al- in a plain adjective that is not of preference, as al-ḍārib “the one who hits” and al-maḍrūb “the one hit”; dhū in the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ; and dhā after the interrogative mā or man.

text.original: وَصِلَةُ أَلِ الْوَصْفُ، وَصِلَةُ غَيْرِهَا إِمَّا جُمْلَةٌ خَبَرِيَّةٌ ذَاتُ ضَمِيرٍ طِبْقٍ لِلْمَوْصُولِ يُسَمَّى عَائِدًا، وَقَدْ يُحْذَفُ نَحْوُ: أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ، وَمَا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ، فَاقْضِ مَا أَنْتَ قَاضٍ، وَيَشْرَبُ مِمَّا تَشْرَبُونَ، أَوْ ظَرْفٌ أَوْ مَجْرُورٌ تَامَّانِ مُتَعَلِّقَانِ بِاسْتَقَرَّ مَحْذُوفًا.
text.en: The ṣila of al- is the adjective. The ṣila of the others is either a declarative sentence (jumla khabariyya) with a pronoun that agrees with the relative, which is called the returner (ʿāʾid) — it may be dropped, as ayyuhum ashaddu “which of them is most severe” [19:69], wa-mā ʿamilat aydīhim “and what their hands have made” [36:35], fa-iqḍi mā anta qāḍin “so decree what you will decree” [20:72] and wa-yashrabu mimmā tashrabūna “and he drinks of what you drink” [23:33] — or an adverb (ẓarf) or a majrūr [phrase], both complete, attached to an understood istaqarra “it is settled”.

lessons.title: The noun with al-, and the noun joined to a definite
body: The fifth kind of definite noun is “the noun with the article”. The article is al- as a whole, “according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, not the lām alone, against al-Akhfash”. Ibn Hishām names the masters on each side because the grammarians argued over it; for the student it is enough that al- makes a noun definite.

Al- has three uses. It may point to what is already known (ʿahd): mentioned just before, fī zujājatin al-zujājatu, “in a glass; the glass …” (Q 24:35), where the second is the glass just named; or known to speaker and hearer, jāʾa al-qāḍī, “the judge came”, the one both know. It may name the kind as such (jins): ahlaka al-nāsa al-dīnāru wa-l-dirhamu, “the dinar and the dirham have destroyed people”, money as a thing, not one coin; wa-jaʿalnā mina al-māʾi kulla shayʾin ḥayyin, “and We made from water every living thing” (Q 21:30).

Or it may take in all (istighrāq): all the individuals, wa-khuliqa al-insānu ḍaʿīfan, “and man was created weak” (Q 4:28), every human being; or all the qualities, Zaydun al-rajulu, “Zayd is the man”, the man in every quality of manhood. The test of istighrāq of individuals is that kull, “every”, could take the place of al-: “every human was created weak”. And “replacing the lām with a mīm is a dialect of Ḥimyar”: am- in place of al-.

The sixth kind is the noun joined by iḍāfa to one of these five. It is definite “according to what it is joined to”: ghulāmu Zaydin, “Zayd's servant”, has the rank of a proper name, ghulāmu hādhā that of a demonstrative. The one exception is the noun joined to a pronoun: ghulāmī, “my servant”, does not reach the rank of the pronoun but is “like the proper name”.

terms.en: al- for what is known already
al- for the kind as such
taking in all: every individual, or every quality
a noun joined to a definite: definite by what it is joined to

examples.en: fī zujājatin al-zujājatu (Q 24:35): al- for what was just mentioned
al- for the kind: money as such
wa-khuliqa al-insānu ḍaʿīfan (Q 4:28): every human being
Zaydun al-rajulu: all the qualities of a man

tasks.prompt: Which use of al- is in each: fī zujājatin al-zujājatu; jāʾa al-qāḍī; wa-khuliqa al-insānu ḍaʿīfan; Zaydun al-rajulu?
tasks.answer: Al-zujājatu: what was just mentioned (ʿahd). Al-qāḍī: what is known to both (ʿahd). Al-insānu: taking in all individuals. Al-rajulu: taking in all qualities.

tasks.prompt: How can you test that the al- of wa-khuliqa al-insānu ḍaʿīfan takes in all individuals?
tasks.answer: Put kull in its place: “every human being was created weak” keeps the meaning. Where kull fits, al- takes in all individuals.

tasks.prompt: How definite is ghulāmu Zaydin, and how definite is ghulāmī?
tasks.answer: Ghulāmu Zaydin has the rank of what it is joined to, a proper name. Ghulāmī is joined to a pronoun, but it does not reach the pronoun's rank: it is “like the proper name”.

quiz.prompt: For al-Khalīl and Sībawayh the article is…
quiz.explanation: Against al-Akhfash, who held it to be the lām alone.

quiz.prompt: In fī zujājatin al-zujājatu, al- is for…
quiz.explanation: The glass named a moment before.

quiz.prompt: In ahlaka al-nāsa al-dīnāru wa-l-dirhamu, al- in al-dīnāru is for…
quiz.explanation: Money as such, not one coin.

quiz.prompt: The test of al- that takes in all individuals is…
options: that kull can take its place
quiz.explanation: “Every human being was created weak.”

quiz.prompt: Zaydun al-rajulu means…
options: Zayd is the man, in every quality of a man
quiz.explanation: Al- that takes in all qualities.

quiz.prompt: Replacing the lām of al- with a mīm is…
quiz.explanation: Am- in place of al-.

quiz.prompt: Ghulāmī, “my servant”, is definite at the rank of…
quiz.explanation: The noun joined to a pronoun is “like the proper name”.

text.original: ثُمَّ ذُو الْأَدَاةِ، وَهِيَ أَلْ عِنْدَ الْخَلِيلِ وَسِيبَوَيْهِ، لَا اللَّامُ وَحْدَهَا خِلَافًا لِلْأَخْفَشِ، وَتَكُونُ لِلْعَهْدِ نَحْوُ: فِي زُجَاجَةٍ الزُّجَاجَةُ، وَجَاءَ الْقَاضِي، أَوْ لِلْجِنْسِ كَأَهْلَكَ النَّاسَ الدِّينَارُ وَالدِّرْهَمُ، وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ،
text.en: Then the noun with the article (dhū al-adāt). The article is al- according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, not the lām alone, against al-Akhfash. It is for what is known [already] (ʿahd), as fī zujājatin al-zujājatu “in a glass; the glass …” [24:35] and jāʾa al-qāḍī “the judge came”; or for the kind (jins), as ahlaka al-nāsa al-dīnāru wa-al-dirhamu “the dinar and the dirham have destroyed people” and wa-jaʿalnā mina al-māʾi kulla shayʾin ḥayyin “and We made from water every living thing” [21:30];

text.original: أَوْ لِاسْتِغْرَاقِ الْأَفْرَادِ نَحْوُ: وَخُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ ضَعِيفًا، أَوْ صِفَاتِهِ نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ الرَّجُلُ. وَإِبْدَالُ اللَّامِ مِيمًا لُغَةٌ حِمْيَرِيَّةٌ.
text.en: or for taking in all the individuals, as wa-khuliqa al-insānu ḍaʿīfan “and man was created weak” [4:28], or all their qualities, as Zaydun al-rajulu “Zayd is the man [indeed]”. Replacing the lām with a mīm is a dialect of Ḥimyar.

text.original: وَالْمُضَافُ إِلَى وَاحِدٍ مِمَّا ذُكِرَ، وَهُوَ بِحَسَبِ مَا يُضَافُ إِلَيْهِ، إِلَّا الْمُضَافَ إِلَى الضَّمِيرِ فَكَالْعَلَمِ.
text.en: And what is muḍāf to one of those mentioned. It is [definite] according to what it is muḍāf to, except what is muḍāf to the pronoun, which is like the proper name.

lessons.title: The subject and the predicate; the indefinite subject; the predicate as a sentence
body: The subject (mubtadaʾ) and the predicate (khabar) are both in rafʿ: Allāhu rabbunā, “God is our Lord”. The subject is what is spoken about; the predicate is what is said of it.

The subject is normally definite, since one speaks of what the hearer knows. An indefinite noun may be a subject “if it is general or made particular”. General: after a negation, mā rajulun fī al-dāri, “no man is in the house”, or a question, a-ilāhun maʿa Allāhi, “is there a god with God?” (Q 27:60). Made particular: by a description, la-ʿabdun muʾminun khayrun min mushrikin, “a believing slave is better than an idolater” (Q 2:221), or by iḍāfa, khamsu ṣalawātin katabahunna Allāhu, “five prayers that God has prescribed”.

The predicate may be a whole sentence, but then it needs a link (rābiṭ) that ties it to the subject. The book gives four: a pronoun, Zaydun abūhu qāʾimun, “Zayd, his father is standing”; a demonstrative, wa-libāsu al-taqwā dhālika khayrun, “but the garment of godfearing, that is best” (Q 7:26); the subject repeated, al-qāriʿatu mā al-qāriʿatu, “the Striking: what is the Striking?” (Q 101:1–2); and a general word that takes in the subject, Zaydun niʿma al-rajulu, “Zayd, how good a man!”, where “the man” includes Zayd.

One kind of sentence needs no link: “except in the like of qul huwa Allāhu aḥadun”, “say: He is God, One” (Q 112:1). There huwa is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the sentence Allāhu aḥadun is the matter itself; a predicate that is its subject in meaning needs nothing to tie it back.

terms.en: the subject: what is spoken about
the predicate: what is said of the subject
the link that ties a predicate sentence to its subject

tasks.prompt: Why can rajulun be a subject in mā rajulun fī al-dāri, and ʿabdun in la-ʿabdun muʾminun khayrun min mushrikin?
tasks.arabic: مَا رَجُلٌ فِي الدَّارِ — لَعَبْدٌ مُؤْمِنٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكٍ
tasks.answer: An indefinite may be a subject if it is general or made particular. Rajulun is general after the negation mā (“no man at all”). ʿAbdun is made particular by its description muʾminun.

tasks.prompt: Find the link in each: Zaydun abūhu qāʾimun; wa-libāsu al-taqwā dhālika khayrun; al-qāriʿatu mā al-qāriʿatu.
tasks.answer: The pronoun -hu in abūhu; the demonstrative dhālika; the subject al-qāriʿatu repeated.

tasks.prompt: Why does the predicate in qul huwa Allāhu aḥadun need no link?
tasks.answer: Huwa is the pronoun of the matter, and the sentence Allāhu aḥadun is that matter itself. A predicate that is its subject in meaning needs nothing to tie it back.

quiz.prompt: The subject and the predicate are both in…
options: the subject in rafʿ, the predicate in naṣb
quiz.explanation: Allāhu rabbunā.

quiz.prompt: An indefinite noun may be a subject if it is…
quiz.explanation: Mā rajulun fī al-dāri; la-ʿabdun muʾminun.

quiz.prompt: In a-ilāhun maʿa Allāhi, the indefinite subject is general because of…
quiz.explanation: After a question, as after a negation, the indefinite is general.

quiz.prompt: In khamsu ṣalawātin katabahunna Allāhu, khamsu is made particular by…
quiz.explanation: Joined to ṣalawātin.

quiz.prompt: In Zaydun abūhu qāʾimun, the link is…
quiz.explanation: The pronoun ties the sentence abūhu qāʾimun to Zayd.

Which predicate sentence needs no link?

quiz.explanation: Huwa is the pronoun of the matter, and the sentence is the matter itself.

text.original: الْمُبْتَدَأُ وَالْخَبَرُ مَرْفُوعَانِ كَاللَّهُ رَبُّنَا. وَيَقَعُ الْمُبْتَدَأُ نَكِرَةً إِنْ عَمَّ أَوْ خَصَّ نَحْوُ: مَا رَجُلٌ فِي الدَّارِ، وَ: أَإِلَهٌ مَعَ اللَّهِ، وَ: لَعَبْدٌ مُؤْمِنٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكٍ، وَ: خَمْسُ صَلَوَاتٍ كَتَبَهُنَّ اللَّهُ.
text.en: The mubtadaʾ and the khabar are both marfūʿ, as Allāhu rabbunā “God is our Lord”. The mubtadaʾ may be indefinite if it is general or made particular, as mā rajulun fī al-dāri “no man is in the house”, a-ilāhun maʿa Allāhi “is there a god with God?” [27:60], la-ʿabdun muʾminun khayrun min mushrikin “a believing slave is better than an idolater” [2:221] and khamsu ṣalawātin katabahunna Allāhu “five prayers that God has prescribed”.

text.original: وَالْخَبَرُ جُمْلَةٌ لَهَا رَابِطٌ كَزَيْدٌ أَبُوهُ قَائِمٌ، وَ: وَلِبَاسُ التَّقْوَى ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ، وَ: الْقَارِعَةُ مَا الْقَارِعَةُ، وَزَيْدٌ نِعْمَ الرَّجُلُ، إِلَّا فِي نَحْوِ: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ.
text.en: The khabar may be a sentence that has a link (rābiṭ), as Zaydun abūhu qāʾimun “Zayd, his father is standing”, wa-libāsu al-taqwā dhālika khayrun “but the garment of godfearing, that is best” [7:26], al-qāriʿatu mā al-qāriʿatu “the Striking: what is the Striking?” [101:1–2] and Zaydun niʿma al-rajulu “Zayd, how good a man [he is]”; except in the like of qul huwa Allāhu aḥadun “say: He is God, One” [112:1].

lessons.title: The predicate as adverb or phrase; putting it first, dispensing with it, dropping it
body: The predicate may be an adverb (ẓarf) in naṣb, wa-l-rakbu asfala minkum, “and the caravan was below you” (Q 8:42), or a preposition with its noun, al-ḥamdu li-llāhi rabbi al-ʿālamīna, “praise be to God, Lord of the worlds” (Q 1:2). Neither is the predicate by itself: both hang on an understood word, mustaqirrun, “settled”, or istaqarra, “it is settled”: “praise is settled for God”. Ibn Hishām gives both, the noun and the verb, since the grammarians differ on which to understand.

“A time is not given as the predicate of a thing”: one may say al-qitālu al-yawma, “the fighting is today”, of an event, but not “Zaydun al-yawma”, since a person is not in a time the way an event is. So al-laylata al-hilālu, “tonight [is] the new moon”, is “to be interpreted”: “the rising of the new moon is tonight”.

The predicate may be dispensed with: when an adjective leans on a question or a negation, its doer fills the predicate's place: a-qāṭinun qawmu Salmā, “are the people of Salmā staying?”; mā maḍrūbun al-ʿAmrāni, “the two ʿAmrs are not beaten”. It may be more than one: wa-huwa al-ghafūru al-wadūdu (Q 85:14); it may come first: fī al-dāri Zaydun, “in the house is Zayd”, and must, when it is a word of question, ayna Zaydun, “where is Zayd?”; and either part may be dropped when it is known: salāmun qawmun munkarūna (Q 51:25), “peace [be upon you]; [you are] people unknown”.

In four places the predicate must be dropped. After lawlā: lawlā antum la-kunnā muʾminīna, “were it not for you, we would have been believers” (Q 34:31), that is, “were you not there”. Before the answer of an explicit oath: la-ʿamruka la-afʿalanna, “by your life [is my oath], I will surely do it”. Before a ḥāl that cannot itself be the predicate: ḍarbī Zaydan qāʾiman, “my hitting Zayd [happens when he is] standing”. And after a wāw of plain accompaniment: kullu rajulin wa-ḍayʿatuhu, “every man [goes together] with his trade”.

terms.en: the understood word an adverb or phrase hangs on: mustaqirr or istaqarra
the adverb, and the preposition with its noun
the necessary dropping of the predicate

examples.en: al-ḥamdu li-llāhi (Q 1:2): the predicate a phrase, hanging on “settled”
a-qāṭinun qawmu Salmā: the doer of the adjective fills the predicate's place
the predicate first: by choice, and of necessity with a word of question
lawlā antum (Q 34:31): the predicate dropped of necessity

tasks.prompt: What is the predicate in al-ḥamdu li-llāhi, and what does it hang on?
tasks.answer: The phrase li-llāhi, a preposition with its noun. It hangs on an understood mustaqirrun or istaqarra: “praise is settled for God”.

tasks.prompt: Why can a time not be the predicate of a person, and how is al-laylata al-hilālu explained?
tasks.answer: An event happens in a time, but a person is not “in” a day in that way, so “Zayd is today” says nothing. Al-laylata al-hilālu is taken to mean “the rising of the new moon is tonight”: the predicate is of an event, the rising.

tasks.prompt: In a-qāṭinun qawmu Salmā, what fills the place of the predicate, and why is that allowed?
tasks.answer: Qāṭinun is the subject and qawmu its doer, which fills the place of the predicate. This is allowed because the adjective leans on the question a-.

quiz.prompt: In al-ḥamdu li-llāhi, li-llāhi hangs on…
quiz.explanation: The adverb and the phrase are not the predicate by themselves.

quiz.prompt: Which is NOT allowed?
options: A time as predicate of a person
quiz.explanation: “A time is not given as the predicate of a thing.”

quiz.prompt: In mā maḍrūbun al-ʿAmrāni, al-ʿAmrāni…
options: fills the place of the predicate
quiz.explanation: The adjective leans on a negation, and its deputy doer fills the predicate's place.

quiz.prompt: The predicate must come first in…
quiz.explanation: A word of question takes the head of the sentence.

quiz.prompt: After lawlā the predicate is…
quiz.explanation: Lawlā antum: “were you not present”.

quiz.prompt: In ḍarbī Zaydan qāʾiman, qāʾiman is…
options: a ḥāl standing before the dropped predicate
quiz.explanation: A ḥāl that cannot itself be the predicate.

quiz.prompt: Salāmun qawmun munkarūna shows…
options: a predicate dropped, then a subject dropped
quiz.explanation: “Peace [upon you]; [you are] a people unknown” (Q 51:25).

text.original: وَظَرْفٌ مَنْصُوبٌ نَحْوُ: وَالرَّكْبُ أَسْفَلَ مِنْكُمْ، وَجَارٌّ وَمَجْرُورٌ كَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، وَتَعَلُّقُهُمَا بِمُسْتَقِرٍّ أَوِ اسْتَقَرَّ مَحْذُوفَيْنِ. وَلَا يُخْبَرُ بِالزَّمَانِ عَنِ الذَّاتِ، وَ«اللَّيْلَةَ الْهِلَالُ» مُتَأَوَّلٌ.
text.en: Or an adverb (ẓarf) in naṣb, as wa-al-rakbu asfala minkum “and the caravan was below you” [8:42]; or a preposition with its majrūr, as al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi rabbi al-ʿālamīna “praise be to God, Lord of the worlds” [1:2]; and both are attached to an understood mustaqirrin “settled” or istaqarra “it is settled”. A time is not given as the khabar of a thing, and al-laylata al-hilālu “tonight [is] the new moon” is to be interpreted [otherwise].

text.original: وَيُغْنِي عَنِ الْخَبَرِ مَرْفُوعُ وَصْفٍ مُعْتَمِدٍ عَلَى اسْتِفْهَامٍ أَوْ نَفْيٍ نَحْوُ: أَقَاطِنٌ قَوْمُ سَلْمَى، وَمَا مَضْرُوبٌ الْعَمْرَانِ. وَقَدْ يَتَعَدَّدُ الْخَبَرُ نَحْوُ: وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ، وَقَدْ يَتَقَدَّمُ نَحْوُ: فِي الدَّارِ زَيْدٌ، وَأَيْنَ زَيْدٌ. وَقَدْ يُحْذَفُ كُلٌّ مِنَ الْمُبْتَدَإِ وَالْخَبَرِ نَحْوُ: سَلَامٌ قَوْمٌ مُنْكَرُونَ.
text.en: The khabar is dispensed with by the marfūʿ of an adjective that leans on a question or a negation, as a-qāṭinun qawmu Salmā “are the people of Salmā staying?” and mā maḍrūbun al-ʿAmrāni “the two ʿAmrs are not beaten”. The khabar may be more than one, as wa-huwa al-ghafūru al-wadūdu “and He is the Forgiving, the Loving” [85:14]; it may come first, as fī al-dāri Zaydun “in the house is Zayd” and ayna Zaydun “where is Zayd?”; and either the mubtadaʾ or the khabar may be dropped, as salāmun qawmun munkarūna “Peace! [You are] people unknown” [51:25].

text.original: وَيَجِبُ حَذْفُ الْخَبَرِ قَبْلَ جَوَابِ لَوْلَا وَالْقَسَمِ الصَّرِيحِ، وَالْحَالِ الْمُمْتَنِعِ كَوْنُهَا خَبَرًا، وَبَعْدَ وَاوِ الْمُصَاحَبَةِ الصَّرِيحَةِ، نَحْوُ: لَوْلَا أَنْتُمْ لَكُنَّا مُؤْمِنِينَ، وَلَعَمْرُكَ لَأَفْعَلَنَّ، وَضَرْبِي زَيْدًا قَائِمًا، وَكُلُّ رَجُلٍ وَضَيْعَتُهُ.
text.en: The khabar must be dropped before the answer of lawlā and of an explicit oath, before a ḥāl that cannot be the khabar, and after a wāw of plain accompaniment, as lawlā antum la-kunnā muʾminīna “were it not for you, we would have been believers” [34:31], la-ʿamruka la-afʿalanna “by your life, I will surely do [it]”, ḍarbī Zaydan qāʾiman “my hitting Zayd [is when he is] standing” and kullu rajulin wa-ḍayʿatuhu “every man [is] with his trade”.

parts.title: What annuls the rule of the subject and predicate

lessons.title: Kāna and its sisters
body: The annullers (nawāsikh) are words that come before a subject and predicate and change their rule. They are of three kinds; the first is kāna and its twelve sisters: amsā, aṣbaḥa, aḍḥā, ẓalla, bāta, ṣāra, laysa, mā zāla, mā fatiʾa, mā infakka, mā bariḥa and mā dāma. They put the subject in rafʿ as their ism and the predicate in naṣb as their khabar: wa-kāna rabbuka qadīran, “and your Lord is powerful” (Q 25:54).

The khabar may come between the verb and its ism: fa-laysa sawāʾan ʿālimun wa-jahūlu, “for one who knows and one who is ignorant are not alike”. It may even come before the verb, except the khabar of dāma and of laysa. The first five, kāna, amsā, aṣbaḥa, aḍḥā and ẓalla, may mean “became”, like ṣāra. And all of them except laysa, fatiʾa and zāla may be complete (tāmm), doing without a khabar: wa-in kāna dhū ʿusratin, “and if there is one in difficulty” (Q 2:280); ḥīna tumsūna wa-ḥīna tuṣbiḥūna, “when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning” (Q 30:17); mā dāmati al-samāwātu wa-l-arḍu, “as long as the heavens and the earth endure” (Q 11:107).

Kāna has four uses of its own. It may be added (zāʾida) in the middle of a sentence, governing nothing: mā kāna aḥsana Zaydan, “how fine Zayd was!”. Its muḍāriʿ in jazm may lose its nūn, lam yaku for lam yakun, as wa-lam aku baghiyyan (Q 19:20), unless a sukūn follows it or an object pronoun is joined to it.

It may be dropped alone, with mā in its place: ammā anta dhā nafarin, “since you are one with a band of men”, for an kunta. And it may be dropped with its ism: in khayran fa-khayrun, “if [the deed was] good, [the reward is] good”; iltamis wa-law khātaman min ḥadīdin, “seek, even [if it be] a ring of iron”. In both, the naṣb of khayran and khātaman is the trace of the dropped kāna.

terms.en: the annullers: words that change the rule of subject and predicate
the ism of kāna (rafʿ) and its khabar (naṣb)
complete kāna: “there was, it happened”, with a doer only
added kāna, which governs nothing

examples.en: wa-kāna rabbuka qadīran (Q 25:54): the ism in rafʿ, the khabar in naṣb
wa-in kāna dhū ʿusratin (Q 2:280): complete kāna, with a doer only
mā kāna aḥsana Zaydan: added kāna
in khayran fa-khayrun: kāna dropped with its ism

tasks.prompt: Give the ism and the khabar, with their states, in wa-kāna rabbuka qadīran.
tasks.answer: Rabbuka is the ism of kāna, in rafʿ (the ḍamma on rabbu); qadīran is its khabar, in naṣb.

tasks.prompt: Why is kāna in wa-in kāna dhū ʿusratin complete, and what does it mean there?
tasks.answer: It has only a doer, dhū ʿusratin, and no khabar; it means “there is, there happens to be”: “and if there is one in difficulty”.

tasks.prompt: Restore what is dropped in in khayran fa-khayrun, and say why khayran is in naṣb.
tasks.answer: In kāna ʿamaluhu khayran fa-jazāʾuhu khayrun: “if his deed was good, his reward is good”. Kāna and its ism are dropped; khayran is its khabar, so it keeps the naṣb.

the subject in rafʿ and the predicate in naṣb
quiz.explanation: Wa-kāna rabbuka qadīran.

quiz.prompt: Whose khabar may NOT come before the verb?
quiz.explanation: The book excepts the khabar of dāma and laysa.

quiz.prompt: Which of these can never be complete?
quiz.explanation: Laysa, fatiʾa and zāla always need a khabar.

quiz.prompt: In ḥīna tumsūna wa-ḥīna tuṣbiḥūna, the verbs are…

quiz.prompt: In mā kāna aḥsana Zaydan, kāna is…

quiz.prompt: Lam aku in wa-lam aku baghiyyan is…

quiz.explanation: The nūn of kāna's muḍāriʿ in jazm may drop (Q 19:20).

it is the object of iltamis
quiz.explanation: “Even if [what you seek] be a ring of iron.”

text.original: النَّوَاسِخُ لِحُكْمِ الْمُبْتَدَإِ وَالْخَبَرِ ثَلَاثَةُ أَنْوَاعٍ: أَحَدُهَا: كَانَ، وَأَمْسَى، وَأَصْبَحَ، وَأَضْحَى، وَظَلَّ، وَبَاتَ، وَصَارَ، وَلَيْسَ، وَمَا زَالَ، وَمَا فَتِئَ، وَمَا انْفَكَّ، وَمَا بَرِحَ، وَمَا دَامَ، فَيَرْفَعْنَ الْمُبْتَدَأَ اسْمًا لَهُنَّ، وَيَنْصِبْنَ الْخَبَرَ خَبَرًا لَهُنَّ، نَحْوُ: وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ قَدِيرًا.
text.en: The annullers (nawāsikh) of the rule of the mubtadaʾ and the khabar are of three kinds. The first: kāna “was”, amsā “became in the evening”, aṣbaḥa “became in the morning”, aḍḥā “became in the forenoon”, ẓalla “was all day”, bāta “was all night”, ṣāra “became”, laysa “is not”, mā zāla, mā fatiʾa, mā infakka and mā bariḥa “did not cease”, and mā dāma “as long as”. They put the mubtadaʾ in rafʿ as their ism, and the khabar in naṣb as their khabar, as wa-kāna rabbuka qadīran “and your Lord is powerful” [25:54].

text.original: وَقَدْ يَتَوَسَّطُ الْخَبَرُ نَحْوُ: فَلَيْسَ سَوَاءً عَالِمٌ وَجَهُولُ، وَقَدْ يَتَقَدَّمُ، إِلَّا خَبَرَ دَامَ وَلَيْسَ. وَتَخْتَصُّ الْخَمْسَةُ الْأُوَلُ بِمُرَادَفَةِ صَارَ، وَغَيْرُ لَيْسَ وَفَتِئَ وَزَالَ بِجَوَازِ التَّمَامِ، أَيِ الِاسْتِغْنَاءِ عَنِ الْخَبَرِ، نَحْوُ: وَإِنْ كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ، حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ، مَا دَامَتِ السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ.
text.en: The khabar may come in the middle, as fa-laysa sawāʾan ʿālimun wa-jahūlu “for one who knows and one who is ignorant are not alike”, and it may come first, except the khabar of dāma and laysa. The first five alone may be used in the sense of ṣāra “became”; and those other than laysa, fatiʾa and zāla alone may be complete, that is, do without a khabar, as wa-in kāna dhū ʿusratin “and if there is one in difficulty” [2:280], ḥīna tumsūna wa-ḥīna tuṣbiḥūna “when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning” [30:17] and mā dāmati al-samāwātu wa-al-arḍu “as long as the heavens and the earth endure” [11:107].

text.original: وَاخْتَصَّتْ كَانَ بِجَوَازِ زِيَادَتِهَا مُتَوَسِّطَةً نَحْوُ: مَا كَانَ أَحْسَنَ زَيْدًا، وَحَذْفِ نُونِ مُضَارِعِهَا الْمَجْزُومِ وَصْلًا إِنْ لَمْ يَلْقَهَا سَاكِنٌ وَلَا ضَمِيرُ نَصْبٍ مُتَّصِلٌ، وَحَذْفِهَا وَحْدَهَا مُعَوَّضًا عَنْهَا مَا فِي مِثْلِ: أَمَّا أَنْتَ ذَا نَفَرٍ، وَمَعَ اسْمِهَا فِي مِثْلِ: إِنْ خَيْرًا فَخَيْرٌ، وَالْتَمِسْ وَلَوْ خَاتَمًا مِنْ حَدِيدٍ.
text.en: Kāna alone may be added (zāʾida) in the middle, as mā kāna aḥsana Zaydan “how fine Zayd was!”; may lose the nūn of its majzūm muḍāriʿ in connected speech, if no sukūn meets it and no attached pronoun in naṣb; may be dropped by itself, with mā in its place, in the like of ammā anta dhā nafarin “since you are one with a band of men”; and may be dropped with its ism, in the like of in khayran fa-khayrun “if [the deed was] good, then [the reward is] good” and iltamis wa-law khātaman min ḥadīdin “seek, even [if it be] a ring of iron”.

lessons.title: Mā, lā and lāta, which resemble laysa
body: “The negating mā is, among the people of the Ḥijāz, like laysa”: it puts its ism in rafʿ and its khabar in naṣb: mā hādhā basharan, “this is not a human being” (Q 12:31). The Banū Tamīm leave it without work, and the Qurʾān here follows the Ḥijāz.

It works only on four conditions. The ism comes first: if the khabar comes first, mā loses its work. No added in follows it: mā in Zaydun qāʾimun leaves mā without work. Nothing governed by the khabar comes before the ism, unless it is an adverb or a prepositional phrase. And the khabar is not joined with illā: wa-mā Muḥammadun illā rasūlun, “Muḥammad is only a messenger” (Q 3:144), has rasūlun in rafʿ, because illā has broken the negation.

Lā works the same way “in verse”, on condition that both its nouns are indefinite: taʿazza fa-lā shayʾun ʿalā al-arḍi bāqiyā / wa-lā wazarun mimmā qaḍā Allāhu wāqiyā, “take comfort, for nothing on earth is lasting, and no refuge shields from what God has decreed”. Bāqiyā and wāqiyā are its khabars, in naṣb (the final alif is the lengthening of the verse).

Lāta works only with ḥīn, “time”, and words like it. Its two parts never appear together, and mostly the one in rafʿ is dropped: wa-lāta ḥīna manāṣin, “and it was no time for escape” (Q 38:3), that is, “the time was not a time of escape”: the ism “the time” is dropped, and ḥīna is the khabar in naṣb.

terms.en: the mā of the Ḥijāz, which works like laysa
lā like laysa: in verse, with indefinite nouns
lā with a tāʾ, working only with ḥīn

examples.en: mā hādhā basharan (Q 12:31): the khabar of mā in naṣb
wa-mā Muḥammadun illā rasūlun (Q 3:144): illā breaks the negation, so mā does not work
wa-lāta ḥīna manāṣin (Q 38:3): the ism dropped, ḥīna the khabar

tasks.prompt: Why is basharan in naṣb in mā hādhā basharan?
tasks.answer: Mā works like laysa in the usage of the Ḥijāz, which the Qurʾān follows here: hādhā is its ism (in the place of rafʿ) and basharan its khabar, in naṣb. All four conditions are met.

tasks.prompt: Why is rasūlun in rafʿ in wa-mā Muḥammadun illā rasūlun?
tasks.answer: Mā works only if its khabar is not joined with illā. Here illā has broken the negation, so mā does not work: Muḥammadun is a subject and rasūlun its predicate, both in rafʿ.

tasks.prompt: Restore the dropped part in wa-lāta ḥīna manāṣin.
tasks.answer: Wa-lāta al-ḥīnu ḥīna manāṣin: “the time was not a time of escape”. The ism in rafʿ, al-ḥīnu, is dropped, as it mostly is; ḥīna is the khabar in naṣb.

quiz.explanation: Mā hādhā basharan (Q 12:31).

options: the khabar of lā, in naṣb
quiz.explanation: Lā works like laysa: shayʾun its ism, bāqiyā its khabar.

text.original: وَمَا النَّافِيَةُ عِنْدَ الْحِجَازِيِّينَ كَلَيْسَ إِنْ تَقَدَّمَ الِاسْمُ، وَلَمْ يُسْبَقْ بِإِنْ، وَلَا بِمَعْمُولِ الْخَبَرِ إِلَّا ظَرْفًا أَوْ مَجْرُورًا، وَلَا اقْتَرَنَ الْخَبَرُ بِإِلَّا، نَحْوُ: مَا هَذَا بَشَرًا.
text.en: The negating mā is, among the people of the Ḥijāz, like laysa, if the ism comes first and is not preceded by in, nor by what the khabar governs unless it is an adverb or a majrūr, and if the khabar is not joined with illā, as mā hādhā basharan “this is not a human being” [12:31].

text.original: وَكَذَا لَا النَّافِيَةُ فِي الشِّعْرِ بِشَرْطِ تَنْكِيرِ مَعْمُولَيْهَا نَحْوُ: تَعَزَّ فَلَا شَيْءٌ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ بَاقِيَا * وَلَا وَزَرٌ مِمَّا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَاقِيَا. وَلَاتَ لَكِنْ فِي الْحِينِ، وَلَا يُجْمَعُ بَيْنَ جُزْأَيْهَا، وَالْغَالِبُ حَذْفُ الْمَرْفُوعِ نَحْوُ: وَلَاتَ حِينَ مَنَاصٍ.
text.en: And likewise the negating lā in verse, on condition that both the words it governs are indefinite, as taʿazza fa-lā shayʾun ʿalā al-arḍi bāqiyā / wa-lā wazarun mimmā qaḍā Allāhu wāqiyā “take comfort, for nothing on earth is lasting, and no refuge shields from what God has decreed”. And lāta [is so too], but only with ḥīn “time”; its two parts are not brought together, and mostly the marfūʿ is dropped, as wa-lāta ḥīna manāṣin “and it was no time for escape” [38:3].

lessons.title: Inna and its sisters; the added mā and the lightened forms
body: The second kind of annuller is six particles, each with its meaning: inna and anna for emphasis; lākinna for correcting a wrong impression (istidrāk); kaʾanna for likening, or for supposing; layta for wishing; and laʿalla for hoping, for fearing, or for giving a reason. They put the subject in naṣb as their ism and the predicate in rafʿ as their khabar, the reverse of kāna.

They govern only “if the particle mā is not joined with them”. With mā they stop governing, and the sentence after them returns to subject and predicate: innamā Allāhu ilāhun wāḥidun, “God is only one God” (Q 4:171), with Allāhu in rafʿ. This mā is called “the stopping mā” (mā al-kāffa). Layta alone may govern or not with it: laytamā Zaydan qāʾimun and laytamā Zaydun qāʾimun are both said.

Some may be lightened, losing the doubling of their nūn. In (inna lightened) may govern or not, like layta with mā. Lākin lightened never governs. An (anna lightened) governs, but its ism, outside the needs of verse, is always a dropped pronoun of the matter, and its khabar is a sentence. If that sentence begins with a conjugated verb that is not a prayer, something must separate it from an: qad, a particle of the future, a negation or law, as in ʿalima an sa-yakūnu minkum marḍā (Q 73:20), where sa- separates them.

Kaʾan lightened also governs; its ism is seldom spoken, and a verb after it is separated by lam or qad: ka-an lam taghna bi-l-amsi, “as if it had not flourished yesterday” (Q 10:24). These separating words keep the lightened an and kaʾan from being mistaken for the an that puts a verb in naṣb.

terms.en: the stopping mā, which ends the work of inna and its sisters
correcting a wrong impression: the meaning of lākinna
anna lightened: its ism the dropped pronoun of the matter
hoping and fearing: meanings of laʿalla

examples.en: innamā Allāhu ilāhun wāḥidun (Q 4:171): mā stops inna, Allāhu in rafʿ
ʿalima an sa-yakūnu (Q 73:20): lightened an, separated from the verb by sa-

tasks.prompt: Why is Allāhu in rafʿ in innamā Allāhu ilāhun wāḥidun?
tasks.answer: The stopping mā is joined to inna, so inna no longer governs. The sentence is again a subject, Allāhu, and a predicate, ilāhun, both in rafʿ.

tasks.prompt: In ʿalima an sa-yakūnu minkum marḍā, where is the ism of an, and why is sa- there?
tasks.answer: An is anna lightened. Its ism is the dropped pronoun of the matter (“that the matter is: there will be…”), and its khabar is the sentence after it. That sentence begins with a conjugated verb, so the particle of the future sa- must separate it from an.

tasks.prompt: With which particle can mā be joined and the particle still govern?
tasks.answer: Layta: laytamā Zaydan qāʾimun and laytamā Zaydun qāʾimun are both allowed. With the others mā stops the work.

quiz.prompt: Inna and its sisters put…
options: the subject in naṣb and the predicate in rafʿ
the subject in rafʿ and the predicate in naṣb
quiz.explanation: The reverse of kāna.

quiz.prompt: Lākinna is for…
quiz.explanation: Al-istidrāk.

quiz.prompt: Which particle may mean fearing?
quiz.explanation: Laʿalla is for hoping and fearing, or for giving a reason.

quiz.prompt: In innamā Allāhu ilāhun wāḥidun, mā…
quiz.explanation: The stopping mā (Q 4:171).

quiz.prompt: Which particle may still govern with mā?
quiz.explanation: Laytamā: both ways.

quiz.prompt: Lākin, lightened, …
quiz.explanation: “As for lākin lightened, it does not govern.”

quiz.prompt: The ism of the lightened an is…
options: a dropped pronoun of the matter
quiz.explanation: Its khabar is a sentence after it.

text.original: الثَّانِي: إِنَّ وَأَنَّ لِلتَّأْكِيدِ، وَلَكِنَّ لِلِاسْتِدْرَاكِ، وَكَأَنَّ لِلتَّشْبِيهِ أَوِ الظَّنِّ، وَلَيْتَ لِلتَّمَنِّي، وَلَعَلَّ لِلتَّرَجِّي وَالْإِشْفَاقِ أَوِ التَّعْلِيلِ، فَيَنْصِبْنَ الْمُبْتَدَأَ اسْمًا لَهُنَّ، وَيَرْفَعْنَ الْخَبَرَ خَبَرًا لَهُنَّ، إِنْ لَمْ تَقْتَرِنْ بِهِنَّ مَا الْحَرْفِيَّةُ نَحْوُ: إِنَّمَا اللَّهُ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ، إِلَّا لَيْتَ فَيَجُوزُ الْأَمْرَانِ، كَإِنِ الْمَكْسُورَةِ مُخَفَّفَةً.
text.en: The second: inna and anna for emphasis, lākinna for correcting [a wrong impression] (istidrāk), kaʾanna for likening or for supposing, layta for wishing, and laʿalla for hoping and fearing, or for giving a reason. They put the mubtadaʾ in naṣb as their ism, and the khabar in rafʿ as their khabar, if the particle mā is not joined with them, as innamā Allāhu ilāhun wāḥidun “God is only one God” [4:171]; except layta, with which both [ways] are allowed, as with in with kasra when it is lightened.

text.original: فَأَمَّا لَكِنْ مُخَفَّفَةً فَتُهْمَلُ، وَأَمَّا أَنْ فَتَعْمَلُ، وَيَجِبُ فِي غَيْرِ ضَرُورَةٍ حَذْفُ اسْمِهَا ضَمِيرَ شَأْنٍ، وَكَوْنُ خَبَرِهَا جُمْلَةً مَفْصُولَةً إِنْ بُدِئَتْ بِفِعْلٍ مُتَصَرِّفٍ غَيْرِ دُعَاءٍ بِقَدْ أَوْ تَنْفِيسٍ أَوْ نَفْيٍ أَوْ لَوْ. وَأَمَّا كَأَنْ فَتَعْمَلُ، وَيَقِلُّ ذِكْرُ اسْمِهَا، وَيُفْصَلُ الْفِعْلُ مِنْهَا بِلَمْ أَوْ قَدْ.
text.en: As for lākin lightened, it does not govern. As for an [lightened], it governs; outside poetic necessity its ism must be dropped, as a pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and its khabar must be a sentence, separated [from an], if it begins with a conjugated verb that is not a prayer, by qad, by [a particle of] the future, by a negation or by law. As for kaʾan, it governs; its ism is seldom mentioned, and the verb is separated from it by lam or qad.

lessons.title: The order in inna's sentence; inna with kasra; the lām
body: The khabar of inna and its sisters may not come between the particle and its ism, unless it is an adverb or a prepositional phrase: inna fī dhālika la-ʿibratan, “in that is surely a lesson” (Q 3:13); inna ladaynā ankālan, “with Us are fetters” (Q 73:12). In both the ism, ʿibratan and ankālan, comes last, in naṣb.

Inna takes a kasra, not anna with a fatḥa, where a whole sentence is needed, since anna turns its sentence into one noun. The book names four places: at the beginning, innā anzalnāhu, “We sent it down” (Q 97:1); after an oath, Ḥā Mīm. wa-l-kitābi al-mubīni. innā anzalnāhu (Q 44:1–3); after a verb of saying that quotes, qāla innī ʿabdu Allāhi, “he said: I am the servant of God” (Q 19:30); and before the lām, wa-Allāhu yaʿlamu innaka la-rasūluhu, “and God knows that you are His messenger” (Q 63:1). In the last, a verb of knowing would call for anna, but the lām in its khabar makes it inna.

That lām, the lām of beginning (lām al-ibtidāʾ), may come with inna with kasra in four places: on its khabar when the khabar comes late (innaka la-rasūluhu); on its ism when the ism comes late (inna fī dhālika la-ʿibratan); on what the khabar governs when that comes in the middle; and on the separating pronoun (al-faṣl), as in inna hādhā la-huwa al-qaṣaṣu al-ḥaqqu, “this is the true story” (Q 3:62).

With the lightened in, when it does not govern, the lām becomes necessary, unless the meaning is clear without it, because it shows that in is the lightened inna and not the in of negation: wa-in kānat la-kabīratan, “and it was indeed hard” (Q 2:143). Without the lām, the hearer could take in as “not”.

terms.en: the lām of beginning, which may come in inna's sentence
the kasra of inna, where a whole sentence is needed
the separating pronoun between subject and predicate
the lightened in that does not govern

examples.en: inna fī dhālika la-ʿibratan (Q 3:13): the khabar a phrase in the middle, the lām on the ism
qāla innī ʿabdu Allāhi (Q 19:30): inna after a verb of saying
innaka la-rasūluhu (Q 63:1): inna before the lām, even after a verb of knowing

tasks.prompt: In inna fī dhālika la-ʿibratan, which is the ism and which the khabar, and why may the khabar come first?
tasks.answer: ʿIbratan is the ism, in naṣb, with the lām of beginning on it; fī dhālika is the khabar. It may come between inna and its ism because it is a prepositional phrase.

tasks.prompt: Why is it innaka and not annaka in wa-Allāhu yaʿlamu innaka la-rasūluhu?
tasks.answer: After a verb of knowing one would expect anna, but the lām of beginning is in the khabar (la-rasūluhu), and inna takes a kasra before the lām.

tasks.prompt: Why is the lām needed in wa-in kānat la-kabīratan?
tasks.answer: In here is the lightened inna and does not govern. Without the lām it could be taken as the in of negation, “it was not hard”; the lām shows that it confirms: “it was indeed hard”.

text.original: وَلَا يَتَوَسَّطُ خَبَرُهُنَّ إِلَّا ظَرْفًا أَوْ مَجْرُورًا نَحْوُ: إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً، إِنَّ لَدَيْنَا أَنْكَالًا. وَتُكْسَرُ إِنَّ فِي الِابْتِدَاءِ نَحْوُ: إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ، وَبَعْدَ الْقَسَمِ نَحْوُ: حم وَالْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ، وَالْقَوْلِ نَحْوُ: قَالَ إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ، وَقَبْلَ اللَّامِ نَحْوُ: وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُ.
text.en: Their khabar does not come in the middle unless it is an adverb or a majrūr, as inna fī dhālika la-ʿibratan “in that is surely a lesson” [3:13] and inna ladaynā ankālan “with Us are fetters” [73:12]. Inna takes a kasra at the beginning, as innā anzalnāhu “We sent it down” [97:1]; after an oath, as Ḥā Mīm wa-al-kitābi al-mubīni innā anzalnāhu “Ḥā Mīm. By the clear Book! We sent it down” [44:1–3]; after saying, as qāla innī ʿabdu Allāhi “he said: I am the servant of God” [19:30]; and before the lām, as wa-Allāhu yaʿlamu innaka la-rasūluhu “and God knows that you are His messenger” [63:1].

text.original: وَيَجُوزُ دُخُولُ اللَّامِ عَلَى مَا تَأَخَّرَ مِنْ خَبَرِ إِنَّ الْمَكْسُورَةِ أَوِ اسْمِهَا، أَوْ مَا تَوَسَّطَ مِنْ مَعْمُولِ الْخَبَرِ أَوِ الْفَصْلِ، وَيَجِبُ مَعَ الْمُخَفَّفَةِ إِنْ أُهْمِلَتْ وَلَمْ يَظْهَرِ الْمَعْنَى.
text.en: The lām may come upon the khabar of inna with kasra when it comes late, or upon its ism [when it comes late], or upon what comes in the middle of what the khabar governs, or upon the separating [pronoun] (faṣl); and it is necessary with the lightened [in] if it does not govern and the meaning is not [otherwise] clear.

lessons.title: The lā that denies the whole kind
body: “Like inna is the lā that denies the whole kind”: it puts its ism in naṣb and its khabar in rafʿ. But it governs only indefinite nouns, and only when they come right after it: lā ṣāḥiba ʿilmin mamqūtun, “no possessor of knowledge is hated”; lā ʿishrīna dirhaman laka, “you have not twenty dirhams”. It denies the kind: not one possessor of knowledge, none at all.

If its ism is a muḍāf, as ṣāḥiba ʿilmin, or like a muḍāf (shabīh bi-l-muḍāf), a word that governs what follows it, as ʿishrīna, which governs dirhaman, the ism is inflected, in naṣb. If it is single, it is fixed on what would be its sign of naṣb: on the fatḥa, lā rajula wa-lā rijāla, “no man and no men”; on the kasra, lā muslimāti, “no Muslim women”; on the yāʾ, lā rajulayni wa-lā muslimīna.

Lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-llāh, “there is no might and no power but in God”, can be read in five ways. With the first fixed on the fatḥa, lā ḥawla, the second may take the fatḥa (lā quwwata), naṣb (lā quwwatan) or rafʿ (lā quwwatun). With the first in rafʿ, lā ḥawlun, lā is no longer this lā, and the second may take the fatḥa or rafʿ, but not naṣb, since there is no fixed ism in naṣb for it to follow.

The adjective of the fixed ism goes the same three ways: lā rajula ẓarīfa, ẓarīfan or ẓarīfun, “there is no witty man”. But the fatḥa is not allowed if lā is not repeated before the second noun, or the adjective is separated from its noun, or it is not single: then the word cannot be built with its noun into one, and only naṣb or rafʿ remain.

terms.en: the lā that denies the whole kind; it works like inna
like a muḍāf: a noun that governs what follows it, as ʿishrīna dirhaman
the single ism of lā, fixed on its sign of naṣb

examples.en: lā ṣāḥiba ʿilmin mamqūtun: the ism a muḍāf, inflected in naṣb
lā ʿishrīna dirhaman laka: the ism like a muḍāf
lā rajula wa-lā rijāla: single, fixed on the fatḥa
lā rajulayni wa-lā muslimīna: fixed on the yāʾ

tasks.prompt: Why is ṣāḥiba inflected in lā ṣāḥiba ʿilmin mamqūtun, while rajula is fixed in lā rajula fī al-dāri?
tasks.arabic: لَا صَاحِبَ عِلْمٍ مَمْقُوتٌ — لَا رَجُلَ
tasks.answer: Ṣāḥiba is a muḍāf (joined to ʿilmin), so it is inflected, in naṣb. Rajula is single, neither muḍāf nor like one, so it is fixed on the fatḥa, its sign of naṣb.

tasks.prompt: Give the five ways of reading lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata, and the one way that is not allowed.
tasks.answer: Lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata; lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwatan; lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwatun; lā ḥawlun wa-lā quwwata; lā ḥawlun wa-lā quwwatun. Not allowed: lā ḥawlun wa-lā quwwatan, since with the first in rafʿ there is nothing in naṣb for the second to follow.

tasks.prompt: On what is the ism fixed in lā muslimāti and in lā muslimīna?
tasks.answer: Lā muslimāti: on the kasra, the sign of naṣb of the plural with alif and tāʾ. Lā muslimīna: on the yāʾ, the sign of naṣb of the sound masculine plural.

quiz.prompt: The lā that denies the whole kind works like…
quiz.explanation: Its ism in naṣb, its khabar in rafʿ.

quiz.prompt: It governs only…
options: indefinite nouns that come right after it
quiz.explanation: Lā ṣāḥiba ʿilmin mamqūtun.

quiz.prompt: In lā ʿishrīna dirhaman laka, ʿishrīna is…
options: like a muḍāf, inflected in naṣb
quiz.explanation: It governs dirhaman, so it is shabīh bi-l-muḍāf.

quiz.prompt: In lā rajula, rajula is…
quiz.explanation: A single ism is fixed on its sign of naṣb.

quiz.prompt: In lā rajulayni, the ism is fixed on…
quiz.explanation: The dual's sign of naṣb is the yāʾ.

quiz.prompt: Which reading of lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata is NOT allowed?
quiz.explanation: With the first in rafʿ, naṣb of the second is not allowed.

quiz.prompt: In lā rajula ẓarīf-, the adjective may take…
quiz.explanation: Lā rajula ẓarīfa, ẓarīfan, ẓarīfun.

text.original: وَمِثْلُ إِنَّ لَا النَّافِيَةُ لِلْجِنْسِ، لَكِنْ عَمَلُهَا خَاصٌّ بِالنَّكِرَاتِ الْمُتَّصِلَةِ بِهَا نَحْوُ: لَا صَاحِبَ عِلْمٍ مَمْقُوتٌ، وَلَا عِشْرِينَ دِرْهَمًا لَكَ. وَإِنْ كَانَ اسْمُهَا غَيْرَ مُضَافٍ وَلَا شِبْهِهِ بُنِيَ عَلَى الْفَتْحِ فِي نَحْوِ: لَا رَجُلَ وَلَا رِجَالَ، وَعَلَى الْكَسْرِ فِي نَحْوِ: لَا مُسْلِمَاتِ، وَعَلَى الْيَاءِ فِي نَحْوِ: لَا رَجُلَيْنِ وَلَا مُسْلِمِينَ.
text.en: Like inna is the lā that denies the whole kind (lā al-nāfiya li-l-jins), but it governs only indefinite nouns joined to it, as lā ṣāḥiba ʿilmin mamqūtun “no possessor of knowledge is hated” and lā ʿishrīna dirhaman laka “you have not twenty dirhams”. If its ism is not muḍāf or like a muḍāf, it is fixed on the fatḥa in the like of lā rajula wa-lā rijāla “no man and no men”, on the kasra in the like of lā muslimāti “no Muslim women”, and on the yāʾ in the like of lā rajulayni wa-lā muslimīna “no two men and no Muslims”.

text.original: وَلَكَ فِي نَحْوِ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ، فَتْحُ الْأَوَّلِ، وَفِي الثَّانِي الْفَتْحُ وَالنَّصْبُ وَالرَّفْعُ، كَالصِّفَةِ فِي نَحْوِ: لَا رَجُلَ ظَرِيفٌ، وَرَفْعُهُ فَيَمْتَنِعُ النَّصْبُ. وَإِنْ لَمْ تَتَكَرَّرْ لَا، أَوْ فُصِلَتِ الصِّفَةُ، أَوْ كَانَتْ غَيْرَ مُفْرَدَةٍ، امْتَنَعَ الْفَتْحُ.
text.en: In the like of lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata “there is no might and no power” you may give the first a fatḥa, and the second a fatḥa, naṣb or rafʿ, as with the adjective in the like of lā rajula ẓarīfun “there is no witty man”; or [you may give] the first rafʿ, and then naṣb [of the second] is not allowed. If lā is not repeated, or the adjective is separated [from its noun] or is not single, the fatḥa is not allowed.

lessons.title: Ẓanna and its sisters: governing, cancelling, suspending
body: The third kind of annuller is the verbs “of the heart” (al-qalbiyyāt): ẓanna, raʾā, ḥasiba, darā, khāla, zaʿama, wajada and ʿalima. They name what happens in the mind, and they put both subject and predicate in naṣb as two objects: raʾaytu Allāha akbara kulli shayʾin, “I held God to be greater than everything”. “Of the heart” leaves out raʾā of the eye and wajada meaning “found” a lost thing, which take one object.

Their work may be cancelled (ilghāʾ): the two nouns go back to rafʿ, as subject and predicate, and the verb stands aside. This is preferred when the verb comes last: al-qawmu fī atharī ẓanantu, “the people are on my track, I thought”; and it is equal either way when the verb comes in the middle: wa-fī al-arājīzi khiltu al-luʾmu wa-l-khawaru, “and in rajaz verses, I fancied, are baseness and weakness”. Cancelling is a choice.

Suspension (taʿlīq) is not a choice. If the verb is followed by a negating mā, lā or in, by the lām of beginning, by the lām of an oath, or by a question, “their governing is necessarily void in the wording”: li-naʿlama ayyu al-ḥizbayni aḥṣā, “so that We might know which of the two parties reckoned better” (Q 18:12). Ayyu is in rafʿ, because a question must stand at the head of its sentence and nothing before it can govern it.

The difference lies in the words “in the wording”. A cancelled verb governs nothing, in wording or in place. A suspended verb still governs the place: the sentence ayyu al-ḥizbayni aḥṣā stands in the place of the two objects of naʿlama, in naṣb, though no naṣb can be heard.

terms.en: the verbs of the heart: ẓanna and its sisters
cancelling: by choice, when the verb comes last or in the middle
suspension: necessary before a negation, a lām or a question; the place still governed

examples.en: raʾaytu Allāha akbara kulli shayʾin: two objects in naṣb
al-qawmu fī atharī ẓanantu: the verb last, its work cancelled
li-naʿlama ayyu al-ḥizbayni aḥṣā (Q 18:12): suspended by a question

diagram.caption: Ẓanna and its sisters: governing, cancelled, suspended (pp. 19–20)

tasks.prompt: Name the two objects in raʾaytu Allāha akbara kulli shayʾin, and the sentence they come from.
tasks.answer: Allāha is the first object, akbara the second, both in naṣb. They come from Allāhu akbaru kulli shayʾin, “God is greater than everything”.

tasks.prompt: Why is al-qawmu in rafʿ in al-qawmu fī atharī ẓanantu? Could it be in naṣb?
tasks.answer: The verb comes last, so its work is cancelled, which is the preferred way: al-qawmu is a subject and fī atharī its predicate. Naṣb is allowed but weaker: al-qawma fī atharī ẓanantu.

tasks.prompt: Show the difference between cancelling and suspension with li-naʿlama ayyu al-ḥizbayni aḥṣā.
tasks.answer: This is suspension: the question ayyu must be at the head of its sentence, so naʿlama cannot govern it in the wording, and ayyu is in rafʿ. But the whole sentence stands in the place of the two objects, in naṣb. A cancelled verb would govern neither wording nor place.

quiz.prompt: The verbs of the heart put subject and predicate in…
quiz.explanation: Raʾaytu Allāha akbara kulli shayʾin.

quiz.prompt: Cancelling (ilghāʾ) is preferred when the verb…
quiz.explanation: Al-qawmu fī atharī ẓanantu.

quiz.prompt: When the verb comes in the middle, cancelling is…
quiz.explanation: Wa-fī al-arājīzi khiltu al-luʾmu wa-l-khawaru.

quiz.prompt: Suspension (taʿlīq) is…
options: necessary before a negation, a lām or a question
quiz.explanation: Their work is “necessarily void in the wording”.

quiz.prompt: In li-naʿlama ayyu al-ḥizbayni aḥṣā, ayyu is in…
quiz.explanation: The question takes the head of its sentence; the verb is suspended.

quiz.prompt: A suspended verb still governs…
options: the place of the sentence after it
quiz.explanation: The sentence stands in the place of the two objects.

quiz.prompt: Which raʾā takes two objects?
quiz.explanation: Raʾā of the eye takes one object.

text.original: الثَّالِثُ: ظَنَّ، وَرَأَى، وَحَسِبَ، وَدَرَى، وَخَالَ، وَزَعَمَ، وَوَجَدَ، وَعَلِمَ الْقَلْبِيَّاتُ، فَتَنْصِبُهُمَا مَفْعُولَيْنِ نَحْوُ: رَأَيْتُ اللَّهَ أَكْبَرَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ. وَتُلْغَى بِرُجْحَانٍ إِنْ تَأَخَّرَتْ نَحْوُ: الْقَوْمُ فِي أَثَرِي ظَنَنْتُ، وَبِمُسَاوَاةٍ إِنْ تَوَسَّطَتْ نَحْوُ: وَفِي الْأَرَاجِيزِ خِلْتُ اللُّؤْمُ وَالْخَوَرُ.
text.en: The third: ẓanna “supposed”, raʾā “held”, ḥasiba “reckoned”, darā “knew”, khāla “fancied”, zaʿama “claimed”, wajada “found” and ʿalima “knew”, those [verbs] of the heart. They put both in naṣb as two objects, as raʾaytu Allāha akbara kulli shayʾin “I held God to be greater than everything”. Their governing may be cancelled, preferably if they come last, as al-qawmu fī atharī ẓanantu “the people are on my track, I thought”, and either way if they come in the middle, as wa-fī al-arājīzi khiltu al-luʾmu wa-al-khawaru “and in rajaz verses, I fancied, are baseness and weakness”.

text.original: وَإِنْ وَلِيَهُنَّ مَا أَوْ لَا أَوْ إِنِ النَّافِيَاتُ، أَوْ لَامُ الِابْتِدَاءِ، أَوِ الْقَسَمِ، أَوِ الِاسْتِفْهَامُ، بَطَلَ عَمَلُهُنَّ فِي اللَّفْظِ وُجُوبًا، وَيُسَمَّى ذَلِكَ تَعْلِيقًا، نَحْوُ: لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصَى.
text.en: If they are followed by the negating mā, lā or in, by the lām of beginning (lām al-ibtidāʾ), by [the lām of] oath or by a question, their governing is necessarily void in the wording; this is called suspension (taʿlīq), as li-naʿlama ayyu al-ḥizbayni aḥṣā “so that We might know which of the two parties reckoned better” [18:12].

parts.title: The doer, its deputy, preoccupation and contention

lessons.title: The doer, and the agreement of its verb
body: The doer (fāʿil) is in rafʿ: qāma Zaydun, “Zayd stood”; māta ʿAmrun, “ʿAmr died”. The second example is chosen with care: ʿAmr did nothing in dying, yet he is the fāʿil, because in naḥw the doer is the one of whom the verb is said, not one who acts. “Its governor does not come after it”: in Zaydun qāma, Zaydun is a subject, and the doer of qāma is a pronoun hidden in it.

No sign of the dual or plural is joined to the verb when the doer is spoken: qāma rajulāni wa-rijālun wa-nisāʾun, as one says qāma rajulun. The forms yataʿāqabūna fīkum malāʾikatun, “angels come to you in turns”, and a-wa-mukhrijiyya hum, “will they drive me out?”, both from ḥadīth, are “irregular”: they follow the dialect that the grammarians call akalūnī al-barāghīth, “the fleas ate me”.

The tāʾ of the feminine is joined to the verb when the doer is feminine: qāmat Hindun; ṭalaʿati al-shamsu. With a real feminine joined to its verb it is necessary. Both ways are allowed in four cases: with a feminine that is figurative, as qad jāʾatkum mawʿiẓatun (Q 10:57), where elsewhere the Qurʾān says fa-man jāʾahu mawʿiẓatun (Q 2:275); with a real feminine separated from the verb, ḥaḍarati al-qāḍiya imraʾatun; with niʿma and biʾsa, niʿmati al-marʾatu Hindun; and with a plural, qālati al-aʿrābu (Q 49:14). The two sound plurals are like their singulars: qāma al-Zaydūna, qāmati al-Hindātu.

Why then is mā qāmat illā Hindun, “none stood but Hind”, not allowed in prose? Because the true doer is a masculine word that has been dropped, aḥadun, “anyone”: “no one stood but Hind”. The doer is dropped only in a few places, which the book names: with the maṣdar, aw iṭʿāmun … yatīman (Q 90:14–15), “or [someone's] feeding an orphan”; in the passive, wa-quḍiya al-amru (Q 2:210); and in asmiʿ bihim wa-abṣir (Q 19:38), where the second bihim is dropped. Elsewhere it is never dropped.

terms.en: the doer: the one of whom the verb is said, in rafʿ
the tāʾ of the feminine on the verb
the real feminine (a woman) and the figurative (a word)
the dialect that marks plural on the verb before its doer

examples.en: qāma Zaydun; māta ʿAmrun: the doer need not act
no sign of dual or plural on the verb
qālati al-aʿrābu (Q 49:14): the tāʾ allowed with a plural
wa-quḍiya al-amru (Q 2:210): the doer dropped in the passive

tasks.prompt: Is ʿAmrun the doer in māta ʿAmrun, though he did nothing? Why?
tasks.answer: Yes. In naḥw the doer is the one of whom the verb is said, coming after it; ʿAmrun is in rafʿ as the fāʿil of māta, whether or not he acted.

tasks.prompt: Why does one say qāma rajulāni and not qāmā rajulāni?
tasks.answer: When the doer is spoken, no sign of the dual or plural is joined to the verb: the verb stays as with one doer. Qāmā rajulāni belongs to the dialect called akalūnī al-barāghīth and is irregular.

tasks.prompt: Why is mā qāmat illā Hindun not allowed in prose?
tasks.answer: The true doer is a dropped masculine word, aḥadun: “no one stood but Hind”. Since the doer is masculine, the verb takes no tāʾ: mā qāma illā Hindun.

quiz.prompt: In māta ʿAmrun, ʿAmrun is…
quiz.explanation: The doer is the one of whom the verb is said.

quiz.prompt: In Zaydun qāma, Zaydun is…
options: a subject; the doer is hidden in qāma
quiz.explanation: The governor of the doer does not come after it.

quiz.prompt: Which is correct, in the usage the book teaches?
quiz.explanation: No sign of dual or plural on the verb when the doer is spoken.

quiz.prompt: The tāʾ is necessary with…
options: a real feminine joined to its verb
quiz.explanation: Qāmat Hindun.

quiz.prompt: Both qad jāʾatkum mawʿiẓatun and jāʾahu mawʿiẓatun are said because mawʿiẓa is…
quiz.explanation: With a figurative feminine both ways are allowed.

quiz.prompt: With the sound plural al-Zaydūna one says…
quiz.explanation: The sound plurals are like their singulars.

quiz.prompt: Where may the doer be dropped?
options: In the passive, as wa-quḍiya al-amru
quiz.explanation: Also with the maṣdar and in asmiʿ bihim wa-abṣir; nowhere else.

text.original: الْفَاعِلُ مَرْفُوعٌ كَقَامَ زَيْدٌ، وَمَاتَ عَمْرٌو، وَلَا يَتَأَخَّرُ عَامِلُهُ، وَلَا تَلْحَقُهُ عَلَامَةُ تَثْنِيَةٍ وَلَا جَمْعٍ، بَلْ يُقَالُ: قَامَ رَجُلَانِ وَرِجَالٌ وَنِسَاءٌ، كَمَا يُقَالُ: قَامَ رَجُلٌ، وَشَذَّ: يَتَعَاقَبُونَ فِيكُمْ مَلَائِكَةٌ بِاللَّيْلِ، أَوَمُخْرِجِيَّ هُمْ.
text.en: The fāʿil is marfūʿ, as qāma Zaydun “Zayd stood” and māta ʿAmrun “ʿAmr died”. Its governor does not come after it, and no sign of the dual or the plural is joined to [the verb]; rather one says qāma rajulāni wa-rijālun wa-nisāʾun “two men, men, women stood”, as one says qāma rajulun “a man stood”; yataʿāqabūna fīkum malāʾikatun bi-al-layli “angels come to you in turns by night” and a-wa-mukhrijiyya hum “and will they drive me out?” are irregular.

text.original: وَتَلْحَقُهُ عَلَامَةُ التَّأْنِيثِ إِنْ كَانَ مُؤَنَّثًا كَقَامَتْ هِنْدٌ، وَطَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ. وَيَجُوزُ الْوَجْهَانِ فِي مَجَازِيِّ التَّأْنِيثِ الظَّاهِرِ نَحْوُ: قَدْ جَاءَتْكُمْ مَوْعِظَةٌ، وَفِي الْحَقِيقِيِّ الْمُنْفَصِلِ نَحْوُ: حَضَرَتِ الْقَاضِيَ امْرَأَةٌ، وَالْمُتَّصِلِ فِي بَابِ نِعْمَ وَبِئْسَ نَحْوُ: نِعْمَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ هِنْدٌ، وَفِي الْجَمْعِ نَحْوُ: قَالَتِ الْأَعْرَابُ، إِلَّا جَمْعَيِ التَّصْحِيحِ فَكَمُفْرَدَيْهِمَا نَحْوُ: قَامَ الزَّيْدُونَ، وَقَامَتِ الْهِنْدَاتُ.
text.en: The sign of the feminine is joined to it if [the fāʿil] is feminine, as qāmat Hindun “Hind stood” and ṭalaʿati al-shamsu “the sun rose”. Both ways are allowed with an explicit [noun] whose femininity is figurative, as qad jāʾatkum mawʿiẓatun “an admonition has come to you” [10:57]; with a real feminine that is separated [from the verb], as ḥaḍarati al-qāḍiya imraʾatun “a woman came before the judge”; with one joined [to it] in the chapter of niʿma and biʾsa, as niʿmati al-marʾatu Hindun “how good a woman is Hind”; and with a plural, as qālati al-aʿrābu “the Bedouins said” [49:14]; except the two sound plurals, which are like their singulars, as qāma al-Zaydūna “the Zayds stood” and qāmati al-Hindātu “the Hinds stood”.

text.original: وَإِنَّمَا امْتَنَعَ فِي النَّثْرِ: مَا قَامَتْ إِلَّا هِنْدٌ؛ لِأَنَّ الْفَاعِلَ مُذَكَّرٌ مَحْذُوفٌ، كَحَذْفِهِ فِي نَحْوِ: أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيمًا، وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ، وَأَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ، وَيَمْتَنِعُ فِي غَيْرِهِنَّ.
text.en: mā qāmat illā Hindun “none stood but Hind” is not allowed in prose only because the fāʿil is a masculine [word] that has been dropped, as it is dropped in the like of aw iṭʿāmun fī yawmin dhī masghabatin yatīman “or feeding, on a day of hunger, an orphan” [90:14–15], wa-quḍiya al-amru “and the matter was decided” [2:210] and asmiʿ bi-him wa-abṣir “how well they will hear and see!” [19:38]; and [dropping it] is not allowed in other than these.

lessons.title: The order of doer and object; the doer of niʿma and biʾsa
body: “The rule is that [the doer] comes right after its governor.” It may come later by choice, the object between: wa-laqad jāʾa āla Firʿawna al-nudhuru, “and warnings came to the people of Pharaoh” (Q 54:41). It must come later in two cases. When the doer holds a pronoun that refers to the object: wa-idhi btalā Ibrāhīma rabbuhu, “and when his Lord tried Abraham” (Q 2:124); the -hu of rabbuhu is Abraham, and a pronoun may not refer to what comes after it both in wording and in rank. And when the object is an attached pronoun and the doer a noun: ḍarabanī Zaydun, “Zayd hit me”.

The object must come after the doer when the doer is an attached pronoun, ḍarabtu Zaydan, “I hit Zayd”; in the verb of wonder, mā aḥsana Zaydan, “how fine Zayd is!”; and when nothing shows which is which: in ḍaraba Mūsā ʿĪsā the iʿrāb of both names cannot be heard, so the first is the doer. “Unlike arḍaʿati al-ṣughrā al-kubrā”, where the meaning shows that the elder suckled the younger, so the object may stand first.

The object may come before the verb itself, by choice, farīqan hadā, “a party He guided” (Q 7:30), or of necessity, when it is a word that must head its sentence: ayyan mā tadʿū, “whichever you call upon” (Q 17:110), where ayyan, a noun of condition, is the object of tadʿū.

With niʿma and biʾsa the doer is of three kinds: a noun with the al- of the kind, niʿma al-ʿabdu, “how good a servant!” (Q 38:30); a noun joined to one that has it, wa-la-niʿma dāru al-muttaqīna, “how good is the abode of the godfearing!” (Q 16:30); or a hidden pronoun explained by a tamyīz that agrees with the one singled out: biʾsa li-l-ẓālimīna badalan, “how bad an exchange for the wrongdoers!” (Q 18:50), where the pronoun in biʾsa is explained by badalan.

terms.en: the doer's rank: right after its verb
putting the object first, by choice or of necessity
the tamyīz that explains the hidden doer of niʿma and biʾsa

examples.en: wa-idhi btalā Ibrāhīma rabbuhu (Q 2:124): the doer must come later
ḍaraba Mūsā ʿĪsā: no sign shows them apart, so the doer comes first
arḍaʿati al-ṣughrā al-kubrā: the meaning shows the doer, so the order is free
niʿma al-ʿabdu (Q 38:30): the doer with the al- of the kind

tasks.prompt: Why must rabbuhu come after Ibrāhīma in wa-idhi btalā Ibrāhīma rabbuhu?
tasks.answer: The doer rabbuhu holds a pronoun, -hu, that refers to the object Ibrāhīma. If the doer came first, the pronoun would refer to a word after it in wording and in rank, which is not allowed.

tasks.prompt: In ḍaraba Mūsā ʿĪsā, who hit whom? Why may the order not change, while it may in arḍaʿati al-ṣughrā al-kubrā?
tasks.arabic: ضَرَبَ مُوسَى عِيسَى — أَرْضَعَتِ الصُّغْرَى الْكُبْرَى
tasks.answer: Mūsā hit ʿĪsā: neither name shows its iʿrāb, so the order alone tells, and the doer must come first. In the second the meaning shows it: the elder suckled the younger, so al-ṣughrā, the object, may come first.

tasks.prompt: Give the three kinds of doer of niʿma and biʾsa, with the book's examples.
tasks.answer: A noun with the al- of the kind: niʿma al-ʿabdu. A noun joined to one with al-: wa-la-niʿma dāru al-muttaqīna. A hidden pronoun explained by a tamyīz: biʾsa li-l-ẓālimīna badalan.

options: the object is an attached pronoun
quiz.explanation: An attached pronoun object joins the verb before a noun doer.

quiz.explanation: When nothing shows which is which, the first is the doer.

quiz.explanation: The meaning shows that the elder suckled the younger.

quiz.explanation: It is the object of tadʿū, put first of necessity.

quiz.explanation: Q 38:30: al- of the kind on the doer.

quiz.explanation: The doer is a hidden pronoun, explained by the tamyīz.

text.original: وَالْأَصْلُ أَنْ يَلِيَ عَامِلَهُ، وَقَدْ يَتَأَخَّرُ جَوَازًا نَحْوُ: وَلَقَدْ جَاءَ آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ النُّذُرُ، وَنَحْوُ: جَاءَ الْخِلَافَةَ أَوْ كَانَتْ لَهُ قَدَرًا * كَمَا أَتَى رَبَّهُ مُوسَى عَلَى قَدَرِ، وَوُجُوبًا فِي نَحْوِ: وَإِذِ ابْتَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ رَبُّهُ، وَضَرَبَنِي زَيْدٌ.
text.en: The rule is that it comes right after its governor. It may come later by choice, as wa-laqad jāʾa āla Firʿawna al-nudhuru “and warnings came to the people of Pharaoh” [54:41], and as jāʾa al-khilāfata aw kānat lahu qadaran / kamā atā rabbahu Mūsā ʿalā qadari “he came to the caliphate, or it was destined for him, as Moses came to his Lord as was decreed”; and of necessity, in the like of wa-idhi ibtalā Ibrāhīma rabbuhu “and when his Lord tried Abraham” [2:124] and ḍarabanī Zaydun “Zayd hit me”.

text.original: وَقَدْ يَجِبُ تَأْخِيرُ الْمَفْعُولِ كَضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا، وَمَا أَحْسَنَ زَيْدًا، وَضَرَبَ مُوسَى عِيسَى، بِخِلَافِ: أَرْضَعَتِ الصُّغْرَى الْكُبْرَى. وَقَدْ يَتَقَدَّمُ عَلَى الْعَامِلِ جَوَازًا نَحْوُ: فَرِيقًا هَدَى، وَوُجُوبًا نَحْوُ: أَيًّا مَا تَدْعُوا.
text.en: The object must sometimes come after [the fāʿil], as ḍarabtu Zaydan “I hit Zayd”, mā aḥsana Zaydan “how fine Zayd is!” and ḍaraba Mūsā ʿĪsā “Mūsā hit ʿĪsā”, unlike arḍaʿati al-ṣughrā al-kubrā “the younger suckled the elder”. It may come before the governor by choice, as farīqan hadā “a party He guided” [7:30], and of necessity, as ayyan mā tadʿū “whichever you call upon” [17:110].

text.original: وَإِنْ كَانَ الْفِعْلُ نِعْمَ أَوْ بِئْسَ فَالْفَاعِلُ إِمَّا مُعَرَّفٌ بِأَلِ الْجِنْسِيَّةِ نَحْوُ: نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ، أَوْ مُضَافٌ لِمَا فِيهِ نَحْوُ: وَلَنِعْمَ دَارُ الْمُتَّقِينَ، أَوْ ضَمِيرٌ مُسْتَتِرٌ مُفَسَّرٌ بِتَمْيِيزٍ مُطَابِقٍ لِلْمَخْصُوصِ نَحْوُ: بِئْسَ لِلظَّالِمِينَ بَدَلًا، وَنَحْوُ: بِئْسَ مَثَلًا الْقَوْمُ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا.
text.en: If the verb is niʿma or biʾsa, the fāʿil is either made definite by the al- of the kind, as niʿma al-ʿabdu “how good a servant!” [38:30]; or muḍāf to what has it, as wa-la-niʿma dāru al-muttaqīna “and how good is the abode of the godfearing!” [16:30]; or a hidden pronoun explained by a tamyīz that agrees with the one specified (makhṣūṣ), as biʾsa li-al-ẓālimīna badalan “how bad an exchange for the wrongdoers!” [18:50] and biʾsa mathalan al-qawmu alladhīna kadhdhabū bi-āyātinā “how bad as an example are the people who denied Our signs!”.

lessons.title: The deputy of the doer, and the passive form
body: “The doer is dropped, and a mafʿūl bihi takes its place in all its rules”: it is put in rafʿ, it comes after the verb, it cannot be left out, and the verb agrees with it. Ḍaraba ʿAmrun Zaydan, “ʿAmr hit Zayd”, becomes ḍuriba Zaydun, “Zayd was hit”. Zayd, once the object, is now the deputy of the doer (al-nāʾib ʿan al-fāʿil).

If the verb has no object, the deputy is an adverb, a prepositional phrase or a maṣdar, “that is specified and conjugable”: julisa fī al-dāri, “sitting was done in the house”; ḍuriba ḍarbun shadīdun, “a hard hitting was done”. Specified (mukhtaṣṣ) means that it says something: a bare ḍarbun, “a hitting”, tells nothing the verb did not already say. Conjugable (mutaṣarrif) means that it can take other states; a word that is always an adverb, as ʿinda, cannot become the deputy.

The verb takes a new form. Its first letter always takes a ḍamma: ḍuriba, yuḍrabu. In the past the letter before the last takes a kasra, ḍuriba; in the muḍāriʿ a fatḥa, yuḍrabu. The second letter shares the ḍamma in verbs that begin with an added tāʾ, taʿallama → tuʿullima, “it was learnt”; the third shares it in verbs that begin with a hamza of connection, inṭalaqa → unṭuliqa.

The hollow verbs qāla and bāʿa have three ways: a pure kasra on the first letter, as in wa-idhā qīla lahum, “and when it is said to them” (Q 2:11); a kasra with a touch of ḍamma (ishmām); or a pure ḍamma. The first is the usage of the Qurʾān and the one to learn.

terms.en: the deputy of the doer: takes its place in the passive
the verb built for the object: the passive
a kasra with a touch of ḍamma, in qīla and bīʿa
specified and conjugable: the conditions of an adverb or maṣdar as deputy

examples.en: ḍuriba Zaydun; yuḍrabu (the forms from the engine): the passive
julisa fī al-dāri: a prepositional phrase as deputy (julisa from the engine)
tuʿullima, unṭuliqa: the ḍamma shared by the second and the third letter
wa-idhā qīla lahum (Q 2:11): the hollow verb with a pure kasra

tasks.prompt: Make ḍaraba ʿAmrun Zaydan passive, and say what each word has become.
tasks.answer: Ḍuriba Zaydun. ʿAmrun, the doer, is dropped; Zaydun, the object, is now the deputy of the doer, in rafʿ; the verb takes the passive form.

tasks.prompt: If the verb has no object, what may be the deputy, and on what conditions?
tasks.answer: An adverb, a prepositional phrase or a maṣdar, on condition that it is specified (it adds a meaning, as ḍarbun shadīdun) and conjugable (it can take other states, unlike ʿinda).

tasks.prompt: Which letters take the ḍamma in tuʿullima and in unṭuliqa?
tasks.answer: In tuʿullima the first and the second (the tāʾ and the ʿayn). In unṭuliqa the first and the third (the hamza and the ṭāʾ). In both the letter before the last takes a kasra.

quiz.prompt: When the doer is dropped, what takes its place first?
quiz.explanation: Only if there is none do the others come in.

quiz.prompt: The deputy of the doer is in…
quiz.explanation: It takes the doer's place in all its rules.

quiz.prompt: The passive past has a kasra on…
quiz.explanation: Ḍuriba: the kasra before the last letter.

quiz.prompt: The passive muḍāriʿ has a fatḥa on…
quiz.explanation: Yuḍrabu: the fatḥa before the last letter.

quiz.prompt: Why can ʿinda not be a deputy of the doer?
options: It is not conjugable: always an adverb
quiz.explanation: The deputy must be mutaṣarrif.

quiz.prompt: In unṭuliqa, which letters take the ḍamma?
quiz.explanation: A verb beginning with a hamza of connection.

quiz.prompt: Wa-idhā qīla lahum shows the hollow passive with…
quiz.explanation: Q 2:11: the pure kasra, the usage of the Qurʾān.

text.original: يُحْذَفُ الْفَاعِلُ فَيَنُوبُ عَنْهُ فِي أَحْكَامِهِ كُلِّهَا مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يُوجَدْ فَمَا اخْتُصَّ وَتَصَرَّفَ مِنْ ظَرْفٍ أَوْ مَجْرُورٍ أَوْ مَصْدَرٍ.
text.en: The fāʿil is dropped, and a mafʿūl bihi takes its place in all its rules; if there is none, then an adverb, a majrūr or a maṣdar that is specified and conjugable (mutaṣarrif).

text.original: وَيُضَمُّ أَوَّلُ الْفِعْلِ مُطْلَقًا، وَيُشَارِكُهُ ثَانِي نَحْوِ: تُعُلِّمَ، وَثَالِثُ نَحْوِ: انْطُلِقَ، وَيُفْتَحُ مَا قَبْلَ الْآخِرِ فِي الْمُضَارِعِ، وَيُكْسَرُ فِي الْمَاضِي، وَلَكَ فِي نَحْوِ: قَالَ وَبَاعَ الْكَسْرُ مُخْلَصًا أَوْ مُشَمًّا ضَمًّا، وَالضَّمُّ مُخْلَصًا.
text.en: The first letter of the verb takes a ḍamma in every case; the second letter of the like of tuʿullima “it was learnt” shares it, and the third of the like of unṭuliqa “[one] set off”. The letter before the last takes a fatḥa in the muḍāriʿ and a kasra in the past. In the like of qāla and bāʿa you may give [the first letter] a pure kasra, a kasra with a touch of ḍamma, or a pure ḍamma.

lessons.title: Preoccupation (ishtighāl)
body: In Zaydun ḍarabtuhu, “Zayd, I hit him”, the verb that could have governed Zayd is “preoccupied” with a pronoun that refers to him. The same holds when the verb governs something of his, Zaydun ḍarabtu akhāhu, “Zayd, I hit his brother”, or reaches him through a preposition, Zaydun marartu bihi, “Zayd, I passed by him”. Zayd may then take two endings. In rafʿ, as a subject, with the sentence after it as its predicate. Or in naṣb, by a verb that is understood and must be dropped, explained by the spoken one: “[I hit] Zayd, I hit him”, “[I humiliated] Zayd, I hit his brother”, “[I passed] Zayd, I passed by him”; then the sentence after it only explains and has no place in the iʿrāb.

Naṣb is preferred in three cases: before a demand, Zaydan iḍribhu, “Zayd, hit him!”, since a demand is not easily a predicate; after a verbal sentence, to match it, wa-l-anʿāma khalaqahā lakum, “and the cattle He created for you” (Q 16:5), after khalaqa al-insāna (Q 16:4); and after a word that mostly comes before verbs, as the hamza of question or the negating mā: a-basharan minnā wāḥidan nattabiʿuhu (Q 54:24); mā Zaydan raʾaytuhu. The rafʿ of wa-l-sāriqu wa-l-sāriqatu fa-qṭaʿū (Q 5:38), before a demand, “is interpreted”: the commentators follow Sībawayh in taking it as a subject whose predicate is dropped, “among what is laid down for you is the thief…”.

Naṣb is necessary after the words that come only before verbs: in Zaydan laqītahu fa-akrimhu, “if you meet Zayd, honour him”; hallā Zaydan akramtahu, “why did you not honour Zayd?”. Rafʿ is necessary where no verb could govern the noun: kharajtu fa-idhā Zaydun yaḍribuhu ʿAmrun, “I went out, and there was Zayd, ʿAmr hitting him”, because the idhā of surprise is followed only by a nominal sentence. The two are equal after a sentence with two faces, nominal in its start and verbal in its predicate: Zaydun qāma abūhu wa-ʿAmran akramtuhu ʿindahu.

Two verses only look like this chapter. In wa-kullu shayʾin faʿalūhu fī al-zuburi, “and everything they did is in the Scriptures” (Q 54:52), faʿalūhu describes shayʾin; naṣb would mean “they did everything in the Scriptures”, which is false. And in a-Zaydun dhuhiba bihi, “was Zayd taken away?”, the verb is passive: no verb could put Zayd in naṣb there.

terms.en: preoccupation: a verb busy with a pronoun of the noun before it
the noun the verb has turned away from
the spoken verb that explains the dropped one
the two-faced sentence: nominal start, verbal predicate

examples.en: Zaydun ḍarabtuhu (rafʿ, a subject) or Zaydan ḍarabtuhu (naṣb, by a dropped verb)
Zaydan iḍribhu: naṣb preferred before a demand
in Zaydan laqītahu: naṣb necessary after a word reserved for verbs
rafʿ necessary after the idhā of surprise

tasks.prompt: Give the two ways of Zaydun ḍarabtu akhāhu, with the iʿrāb of each.
tasks.answer: Zaydun in rafʿ: a subject, and ḍarabtu akhāhu its predicate (in the place of rafʿ). Zaydan in naṣb: the object of a dropped verb such as ahantu, “I humiliated”, explained by ḍarabtu akhāhu, which then has no place in the iʿrāb.

tasks.prompt: Why is naṣb necessary in in Zaydan laqītahu fa-akrimhu?
tasks.answer: In, the particle of condition, comes only before a verb. So a verb must be understood after it, “in laqīta Zaydan”, and Zaydan is its object, in naṣb.

tasks.prompt: Why is wa-kullu shayʾin faʿalūhu fī al-zuburi not a case of preoccupation?
tasks.answer: Faʿalūhu is a description of shayʾin, not a verb that could govern kullu. The predicate is fī al-zuburi: “everything they did is in the Scriptures”. Naṣb would make it “they did everything in the Scriptures”, which is false.

quiz.prompt: In Zaydun ḍarabtuhu, the verb is “preoccupied” with…
quiz.explanation: The -hu refers to Zayd.

quiz.prompt: Naṣb is preferred in…
